summary: Finished revision of the existing 528-target planning pass. The reader gives all eight layers in dependency order, with the current exact statements, hypotheses, proof routes, APIs, discriminating tests, source locators and consumer contracts. The four/five-parameter genus-one locus, generic evaluation-image positivity, positive surface twist, fixed integral determinant degree, exact early Picard/Hodge imports and Pic(T)-torsors of lifts agree throughout. All eight stages and the six-consumer key remain partial with twenty mathematical gaps, 140 supplier requests and explicit geometric prototype omissions. Current upstream AlgebraicVectorBundles supplies ordinary determinants; moduli-specific descent and ordered clutching comparisons remain scoped inputs. Historical independent review is retained for the next reviewer. No new target, acceptance verdict or implementation claim is introduced.

nodes.title: Moduli stacks of pointed curves
nodes.statement: For integers g,n≥0 with 2g−2+n>0, define a single moduli pseudofunctor CurvesModuli(ε,g,n), ε=smooth or stable, on schemes. Its fibre over S is the groupoid of parent curve families f:C→S, proper flat finitely presented of pure relative dimension one, with geometrically connected fibres of arithmetic genus g and an ordered list of n disjoint sections through the relative smooth locus. In the stable flavour fibres are nodal and ω_{C/S}(Σsᵢ) is relatively ample; the smooth flavour is the full subcategory with f smooth. Arrows are marking-preserving S-isomorphisms; pullback is scheme-theoretic base change with its canonical associator. Write M_{g,n} and M̄_{g,n}. This is a groupoid-valued functor; no coarse or fine representability is built into its definition.
hypotheses: g,n are nonnegative integers and 2g−2+n>0, with the inequality interpreted in the integers.

The base S is an arbitrary scheme. The parent supplies the family predicates; its locally Noetherian cohomology and duality theorems require the separate arbitrary-base extension recorded in the gaps.
proofSteps: Use the parent’s stable-pointed and smooth-curve family data, without redefining stability.
Form the fibre groupoid using marking-preserving relative isomorphisms.
Use pullback universal properties to obtain coherent reindexing; the effective-descent assertion is a separate node.
acceptance: The genus-zero stable range begins at n=3; a two-pointed rational curve is excluded.
A self-node contributes two normalization flags to stability.

sources.locator: Definitions1.1–1.2,printedpp.162–164 (PDF2–4); groupoid statement p.164
sources.match: Definition1.1 specifies stable pointed families; Definition1.2 gives cartesian marking-preserving morphisms and states the groupoid-fibred stack property. The log-dualizing ampleness formulation is imported from the parent roadmap.

api.name: CurvesModuli.obj
api.statement: The fibre groupoid over S has precisely the parent smooth/stable pointed families as objects.

api.name: CurvesModuli.iso
api.statement: Morphisms are exactly S-isomorphisms carrying every ordered marking to the marking of the same index.

api.name: CurvesModuli.pullback
api.statement: For T→S pull back the family and every section; identity and composition agree via coherent canonical isomorphisms.

api.name: CurvesModuli.smoothInclusion
api.statement: For 2g−2+n>0 the smooth flavour is the full open substack of the stable flavour on families whose structure morphism is smooth; base change identifies this inclusion with the smooth-family locus.

api.name: CurvesModuli.geometricPoints
api.statement: Over an algebraically closed field the objects and automorphism groups are those of pointed curves, not only isomorphism classes.

api.name: CurvesModuli.rationalThreeEquivalence
api.statement: For every base scheme S, (M₀,₃)_S≅S≅(M̄₀,₃)_S, with unique trivialization of the universal family as (P¹_S;0,1,∞).

api.name: CurvesModuli.crossRatio
api.statement: Over Spec Z, M₀,₄≅P¹_Z minus {0,1,∞} and M̄₀,₄≅P¹_Z, compatibly with the smooth inclusion and the ordered cross-ratio coordinate.

api.name: CurvesModuli.stableStackProperties
api.statement: For g,n≥0 and 2g−2+n>0, M̄_{g,n} is proper smooth Deligne–Mumford over Spec Z of relative dimension 3g−3+n, and M_{g,n} is its open dense smooth-family locus.

api.name: CurvesModuli.universalForgetful
api.statement: For 2g−2+n>0, M̄_{g,n+1}≅Z̄_{g,n} over M̄_{g,n}; the universal projection is forgetting the last marking and stabilizing, with its n sections given by expansion when the arbitrary extra section equals an old marking.

api.name: CurvesModuli.forgetStabilize
api.statement: For n≥1 and 2g−2+(n−1)>0, forgetting one marking and applying the parent stabilization gives M̄_{g,n}→M̄_{g,n−1}, canonically compatible with base change, label permutations and repeated forgetting; a rational tail with two markings contracts when one of those markings is forgotten.

tests.name: CurvesModuli.rationalThree
tests.statement: Over an algebraically closed field the smooth three-pointed rational curve has a unique isomorphism to (P¹;0,1,∞) and trivial automorphism group.

tests.name: CurvesModuli.rationalTwoExcluded
tests.statement: (P¹;0,∞) fails the stable-range condition and has a positive-dimensional automorphism group.

tests.name: CurvesModuli.ellipticInvolution
tests.statement: In characteristic zero a pointed elliptic curve (E,0) has the nontrivial automorphism [−1]; its fibre groupoid is not a discrete set.

tests.name: CurvesModuli.selfNodeFlags
tests.statement: An irreducible rational nodal curve with one smooth marking is stable of arithmetic genus one: the normalization has three special flags.

tests.name: CurvesModuli.crossRatioBoundary
tests.statement: Over an algebraically closed field, M₀,₄ is P¹ minus {0,1,∞}, M̄₀,₄ is P¹, and its three boundary points are the three unordered 2+2 partitions of the four ordered labels.

tests.name: CurvesModuli.stableStackDimensions
tests.statement: The proper smooth Deligne–Mumford stack M̄_{g,n} has relative dimension 3g−3+n in the stable range: dimension zero for (0,3) and one for (0,4) and (1,1); its smooth-family locus is open.

tests.name: CurvesModuli.universalRationalFour
tests.statement: (M̄₀,₄)_k→(M̄₀,₃)_k=Spec k is the universal curve P¹_k; its three universal marking sections are the boundary points 0,1,∞, and forgetting the fourth mark contracts the inserted two-marked rational tail there.

tests.name: CurvesModuli.forgetRationalTail
tests.statement: Attach a rational tail with two distinct markings to a smooth genus-two component at one point. Forget one tail marking: stabilization contracts the tail, carries the retained tail marking to the attachment, and preserves the genus-two component.

uses.how: One shared definition for smooth and stable pointed families, their automorphisms and classifying maps.
Unpointed genus≥2 moduli and full-level universal curves.
Pointed moduli bases for boundary, Hurwitz and versal-family constructions; the consumer-specific constructions remain in their owners.

nodes.title: Pullback coherence for pointed moduli
nodes.statement: The canonical isomorphisms (C×_S T)×_T U≅C×_S U and C×_S S≅C preserve all markings and satisfy the pentagon and unit identities, defining the moduli pseudofunctor on arbitrary schemes.
hypotheses: g,n≥0 and 2g−2+n>0; composable morphisms U→T→S of arbitrary schemes.
Each family and its ordered markings is as in CurvesModuli; preservation of the arbitrary-base family conditions is an explicit open import.
proofSteps: Use the native scheme pullbacks and pullbackLeftPullbackSndIso with its two projection formulas. For identity base change use the first pullback projection with an identity right leg. Equal projections give equality by pullback.hom_ext, so the pentagon, unit and marking coherence follow by uniqueness.
Import the parent’s base-change preservation of geometric genus, nodality, smooth sections and log-dualizing ampleness.
acceptance: Composition is coherent, not asserted definitionally equal.

sources.locator: Definition1.2,printedp.164 (PDF4),condition(ii)
sources.match: Condition(ii) identifies the source family with the scheme-theoretic pullback. The identity and associativity coherence follow from uniqueness with fixed pullback projections.

nodes.title: Effective descent of pointed stable curves
nodes.statement: CurvesModuli(ε,g,n) has effective fppf descent of objects and isomorphisms, hence is a stack; compare with Mathlib’s pseudofunctor IsStack predicate rather than asserting this predicate supplies an algebraic atlas.
hypotheses: g,n≥0 and 2g−2+n>0; ε is smooth or stable.
Use the fppf topology on schemes, retaining marking-preserving isomorphisms and their cocycle.
proofSteps: Descend the relatively ample log-dualizing line with the family by polarized-scheme descent.
Descend the ordered sections and their disjoint smooth-locus condition.
Use the parent’s geometric-fibre and base-change characterizations to descend the fixed-genus and stability conditions.
acceptance: Do not replace the fibre groupoid by isomorphism classes before descent.

sources.locator: Definition 1.2, printed p.164 (PDF4), groupoid-fibred stack assertion
sources.match: Knudsen calls this a stack and refers to Deligne–Mumford Definition 4.1; the latter paper specializes its general site to the étale topology on p.98. The fppf assertion here is a strengthening using the explicitly requested effective fppf descent of polarized schemes and sections, together with locality of the family conditions; it is not asserted as the printed topology or as a consequence of the IsStack class alone.

nodes.title: The universal curve with an arbitrary extra section
nodes.statement: Define Z̄_{g,n} over M̄_{g,n} by an object (C/S;s₁,…,sₙ;Δ), where Δ:S→C is an arbitrary additional section. It may hit a node or an old marking. For S→M̄_{g,n} classified by C/S, the fibre product S×_{M̄} Z̄ is canonically C. This representable proper flat nodal morphism is the universal curve; its base change to M_{g,n} is a smooth proper curve, and over M̄_{g,n} its relative smooth locus is the open complement of the fibre nodes.
hypotheses: g,n≥0 and 2g−2+n>0; S is an arbitrary scheme and C/S is a stable ordered n-pointed family.
proofSteps: The groupoid of pairs (T→S, a section of C_T/T) is the representable fibre category of C.
Use its universal property to construct the canonical relative scheme and pullback square.
The smooth-universal family is the base change to M_{g,n}; the universal total stack can be smooth over Z even though its projection is nodal.
acceptance: The universal projection is not a smooth morphism at a node.

sources.locator: Introduction,printedpp.1–2,cartesian universal-curve diagram

tests.name: UniversalCurve.nodalProjection
tests.statement: Let C/k be an irreducible rational curve with one ordinary node and one smooth marking over an algebraically closed field. Its arithmetic genus is one and it is pointed-stable. The base change of the universal projection to its classifying point is C→Spec k and is not smooth at the node; smoothness of the total universal stack over Z does not make this projection smooth.

uses.how: Given such C/S with old markings sᵢ and arbitrary extra section Δ, put D=Σsᵢ and J=I_Δ. Let p:J∨⊕O_C(D)→K be the cokernel of the diagonal map h↦(h,h), and put C^s=Proj_C Sym K. Set L_s=K/p(J∨) and L_Δ=K/p(O_C(D)). The canonical invertible quotients sᵢ*K→sᵢ*L_s and Δ*K→Δ*L_Δ give the ordered lifted markings. On the stated locally Noetherian bases the construction commutes canonically with base change and with pointed isomorphisms; the arbitrary-base extension is a recorded gap. On geometric fibres it is an isomorphism at a disjoint smooth new point, inserts a rational tail at a collision, and inserts a rational bridge at a node.

For the universal stable pointed curve f:C→M̄_{g,n}, define Lᵢ=sᵢ*ω_{C/M̄}. Each is an invertible sheaf because the marking is in the relative smooth locus; it identifies with sᵢ*Ω¹_{C/M̄}. Base change and relabelling preserve this line. The class ψᵢ=c₁(Lᵢ) is an exported input to the consumer’s tautological Chow-ring construction, not a new Chow theory here.

For g≥2 choose a representable finite surjective morphism V→M̄_g with V a normal integral scheme projective over Z. Pull back the universal stable curve to V. This is a chosen cover with a stable family, not a new fine moduli interpretation of V.

For the universal stable pointed family f:C→M̄_{g,n}, define E_{g,n}=f_*ω_{C/M̄}. It is locally free of rank g, including rank zero for g=0, and formation commutes with arbitrary base change with its canonical cocycle. The relative dualizing sheaf is untwisted by the markings.

nodes.title: Tricanonical Hilbert polynomial and frame rank
nodes.statement: Apply the parent’s pluricanonical vanishing, very-ampleness and cohomology/base-change API to a stable genus-g curve, g≥2. Its tricanonical direct image has rank 5g−5, the canonical embedding is into P_S(f_*ω³), of relative projective dimension 5g−6, becoming an embedding into P^{5g−6}_S after a local projective frame, its degree is 6g−6 and its Hilbert polynomial is (6t−1)(g−1). These are the numerical inputs to the Hilbert moduli construction, not a second development of the parent’s curve cohomology.
hypotheses: g≥2; every curve family is stable, unpointed, proper, flat and finitely presented with geometrically connected nodal genus-g fibres.
The base-general conclusion requires the stated foundational and arbitrary-base approximation inputs; parent cohomology/duality results have locally Noetherian base scope.
proofSteps: Use the parent’s m≥2 vanishing and m≥3 very-ampleness, and the requested arbitrary-base extension, to obtain locally free direct images and their compatible evaluation embedding.
Compute the degree of ω³ from deg ω=2g−2 and its Hilbert polynomial and rank by the parent’s Riemann–Roch.
acceptance: For m=3 the rank is 5g−5 and the projective dimension is 5g−6.

sources.locator: Theorem 1.2 and its corollary, printed pp.77–78 (PDF4–5)

nodes.title: The tricanonical Hilbert locus
nodes.statement: For g≥2 put r=5g−5 and E=f_*ω_{C/S}³. Define U_g as the locally closed Hilbert subscheme of P^{r−1}_Z representing isomorphism classes of stable genus-g families C/S equipped with an S-isomorphism α:P_S(E)≅P^{r−1}_S. The embedded curve is obtained by composing the complete tricanonical embedding C→P_S(E) with α. It has Hilbert polynomial (6t−1)(g−1). On an embedded family, O_C(1) identifies with ω_{C/S}³ up to tensoring by the pullback of an invertible sheaf from S; no trivialization of that base line is part of the projective-frame data. Impose the canonical relative polarization and complete-projective-frame condition, not just the Hilbert polynomial.
hypotheses: g≥2 and r=5g−5; projective bundles parametrize rank-one quotients of E.
S is an arbitrary scheme; the extension of the parent locally Noetherian direct-image/base-change theory remains an explicit gap.
proofSteps: Use the parent tricanonical evaluation embedding C→P_S(f_*ω³) and the fixed-polynomial universal flat Hilbert family.

Construct the stable locally closed Hilbert locus with the complete canonical relative polarization. Compare O_C(1)⊗ω^{-3} with a base line, retaining that line in descent; a projective frame need not lift to a linear frame.

Use relative Hilbert/Isom representability and the projective-frame functor to identify U_g; changing α defines the PGL_r action. The required relative-polarization and projective-bundle comparison inputs are requested explicitly.
acceptance: A curve with the same Hilbert polynomial but the wrong polarization is excluded.

Proposition 5.1 identifies the atlas fibre with the projective-bundle Isom scheme. The twist test is an explicit deduction using the central GL_r→PGL_r quotient, not a printed example.

nodes.statement: The stable-curve Isom scheme is unramified over its base, including in positive characteristic; its geometric tangent spaces at automorphisms vanish.

nodes.title: Properness of stable-curve Isom
nodes.statement: The stable-curve Isom scheme is proper over the base. For a trait any generic-fibre isomorphism between stable models extends uniquely; do not require the generic fibre to be smooth in the final theorem.
hypotheses: g≥2; every curve family is stable, unpointed, proper, flat and finitely presented with geometrically connected nodal genus-g fibres.
The base-general conclusion requires the stated foundational and arbitrary-base approximation inputs; parent cohomology/duality results have locally Noetherian base scope.
proofSteps: Reduce locally on S to the universal pair of Hilbert families over U_g×U_g using tricanonical projective frames. Under the framed representing property, the scheme of isomorphisms between that universal pair is U_g×PGL_r, r=5g−5: an isomorphism φ:C₁→C₂ induces P(E₁)→P(E₂), and its unique frame change is α₂ P(φ) α₁⁻¹; conversely a frame change gives the corresponding embedded isomorphism. This is the action-groupoid description, not just a statement about orbit classes or the density of U_g×U_g.

The source open consisting of smooth curves is U_g^sm×PGL_r. Independent versal node-smoothing parameters make U_g^sm dense; the smooth projection U_g×PGL_r→U_g is open and surjective, so this inverse image is dense. The source is of finite type over the Noetherian scheme U_g×U_g.

Apply the refined Noetherian scheme criterion of Stacks tag 0208: it suffices to extend maps from generic points of irreducible components of the universal Isom source over DVRs. Those generic points lie in the displayed smooth-curve open. The parent unpointed smooth-generic stable-model uniqueness gives the unique extension. This does not apply a field-extension existence criterion for stacks to a scheme.

Pull back this proper universal Isom scheme to arbitrary pairs of stable families after their local projective frames; properness is local on the target and stable under base change. The family/cohomology approximation input remains explicit. Its valuative consequence then supplies extension for every valuation ring and for nodal generic fibres as well; no such general uniqueness is assumed in the smooth-generic test.
acceptance: The final Isom theorem includes singular generic stable curves.
The universal Isom scheme is the action groupoid U_g×PGL_r, whose smooth-curve open is dense. Density of the ambient pair space alone cannot justify testing only smooth-generic isomorphisms.

sources.locator: Theorem 1.11 proof p.84 (PDF11), Lemma 1.12 pp.84–85 (PDF11–12)

nodes.title: Vanishing of stable-curve obstruction space
nodes.statement: For a proper geometrically connected nodal curve C over an algebraically closed field k, Ext²_{O_C}(Ω¹_{C/k},O_C)=0. The local-to-global map Ext¹_{O_C}(Ω¹_{C/k},O_C)→⊕_{x a node} Ext¹_{O_{C,x}}(Ω¹_{C/k,x},O_{C,x}) is surjective.
hypotheses: C/k is proper, geometrically connected, nodal and pure one-dimensional; k is algebraically closed.
Ext is coherent-sheaf Ext on C; its local terms use the stalk of Ω¹_{C/k}.
proofSteps: Use the lci nodal two-term resolution and local Ext sheaves supported at finitely many nodes.
Apply the local-to-global Ext spectral sequence and H²=0 on curves; H¹ of a finite-support sheaf vanishes.
acceptance: Obstructions vanish, while one independent smoothing parameter remains per node.

sources.locator: Lemma 1.3 p.79 (PDF6), and Proposition 1.5 with proof pp.81–82 (PDF8–9)

Proposition 1.5 proves surjectivity onto the finite set of local singularity deformation spaces. Proper nodal curves meet these hypotheses; the generic coherent Ext package is still a supplier obligation.

nodes.title: Independent node-smoothing parameters
nodes.statement: For a geometric stable genus-g curve g≥2 with r nodes, a versal deformation over the complete unramified coefficient ring has formally smooth base with 3g−3 variables and local node equations uv=tᵢ for r distinct parameters; the framed base has an additional dim PGL(5g−5) smooth factor. The parameters are chart-local and may be permuted by stabilizers.
hypotheses: k is algebraically closed; C/k is stable, unpointed and of genus g≥2, with r nodes.
The coefficient ring is k in characteristic zero and the complete unramified Cohen ring with residue k in characteristic p; node branches are split over k.
Use a deformation with a fixed identification of its special fibre with C; stabilizers still act on this chart.
proofSteps: The local node deformation has one smoothing coordinate per node.
Surjectivity of the global-to-local tangent map and obstruction vanishing give a smooth lifting map.

Use curve Riemann–Roch and duality on the normalization: with total component genus G, v components and r nodes, the branches contribute 2r marked points, and the tangent spaces preserving them have total dimension 3G−3v+2r. Adding r independent local smoothing parameters and g=G+r−v+1 gives 3g−3. Algebraize the deformation with its ample ω³ and use the projective-frame torsor for the additional PGL_r smooth factor, where the frame rank is 5g−5.
acceptance: An automorphism can permute node parameters; no globally chosen ordering of nodes is asserted.

sources.locator: Proposition 1.5 pp.81–82 (PDF8–9), following universal formal deformation and framed comparison pp.82–83; Theorem 1.6 p.83 (PDF10)

nodes.title: The binary quadratic node form
nodes.statement: For a commutative ring A and γ,δ∈A define q_{γ,δ}(x,y)=x²+γxy+δy². Its nondegeneracy condition is that γ²−4δ is a unit. Over a field this describes a possibly nonsplit ordinary double point, including characteristic two. The definition is the polynomial form; the discriminant condition is an explicit hypothesis, not an arbitrary predicate field.

Let Λ be complete noetherian local with residue field k and let q over k have unit discriminant. The pointed node k[[x,y]]/(q), with x,y↦0, has a formally versal hull A_pd=Λ[[s,t]] and R_pd=A_pd[[x,y]]/(q̃(x,y)−q̃(s,t)), with section x↦s,y↦t. The tangent map is an isomorphism k²→k². This is a hull, not a claim that the deformation groupoid is represented by a fine scheme.

For a commutative ring A and γ,δ,x,y,s,t∈A define Φ=((δy+δt+γx,x+s+γt);(−(x−s),y−t)) and Ψ=((y−t,−(x+s+γt));(x−s,δy+δt+γx)). nodes.statement: Set q=X²+γXY+δY², F=q(X,Y)−q(s,t), R=A[Y][X]/(F), u=[X], v=[Y], ι:A→R, c=u−ιs, d=v−ιt, b=u+ιs+ιγ·ιt, a=ιδ·v+ιδ·ιt+ιγ·u, J=(c,d), D=Hom_R(J,R). ev∘ι=id_A, ker(ev)=J, and 0→J→R→A→0 splits A-linearly by ι.

proofSteps: Use the built AdjoinRoot.induction_on to represent r by a bivariate polynomial P. The built lift_mk and eval₂_evalRingHom identify section evaluation with (P.eval(C s)).eval t.

The built Polynomial.mem_span_C_X_sub_C_X_sub_C_iff_eval_eval_eq_zero puts every vanishing representative in span{C(Y−t),X−C(s)}. This already proves the two-variable division statement; do not plan a private generic remainder lemma.
Map that ideal through the actual AdjoinRoot.mk using Ideal.mem_map_of_mem and Ideal.map_span. Its two generator images are v−ιt and u−ιs, so the image lies in J.
Conversely both generators evaluate to zero. Ideal.span_le puts J in the actual evaluation kernel. AdjoinRoot.lift_of and evaluation on constants give ev∘ι=id_A.

The A-linear splitting is made explicit by the separate section-evaluation-split construction. This proof does not use a normal-form basis, noetherianity, a unit discriminant or flatness of a coefficient map.

proofSteps: Compose the checked normal equivalence with the native A-linear second projection. The pairs (0,α) prove surjectivity and ε has pair (0,1).
The inverse formula identifies zero residue exactly with maps j↦rj. The separate actual multiplication construction is injective by regularity of d.
Apply the independently derived correction/scalar-action formula to identify ρ(zh)=ev(z)ρ(h).
For nonzero A, a purported R-linear splitting has dσ(1)=σ(ev(d))=σ(0)=0. Pointwise regularity forces σ(1)=0, contradicting its right inverse property.
acceptance: For nonzero A, there is no R-linear section of ρ: d kills A but acts injectively on D.

nodes.statement: Given such C/S with old markings sᵢ and arbitrary extra section Δ, put D=Σsᵢ and J=I_Δ. Let p:J∨⊕O_C(D)→K be the cokernel of the diagonal map h↦(h,h), and put C^s=Proj_C Sym K. On the stated locally Noetherian bases the construction commutes canonically with base change and with pointed isomorphisms; the arbitrary-base extension is a recorded gap. Trivialize the genus-zero family locally and use the unique three-point projectivity; descend the unique trivialization.
acceptance: The automorphism group of the ordered triple is trivial.

nodes.title: Pointed induction for genus at least two
nodes.statement: For g≥2 and n≥0, M̄_{g,n} is smooth proper Deligne–Mumford over Z of relative dimension3g−3+n with dense smooth locus and relative normal-crossings boundary.
hypotheses: g≥2 and n≥0; all markings are ordered and the universal curve is the stable compactified universal curve.
proofSteps: Induct from the unpointed stack using the universal-curve equivalence.

Use the formal nodal chart: tⱼ↦xy gives the total-space chart with x,y in place of tⱼ, hence smoothness. The pointed boundary is not just the inverse image of the old boundary: it is that inverse image union the n disjoint old-section images, corresponding to rational-tail collisions. The projection is smooth near those images, which are relative Cartier divisors; the node charts handle the remaining intersections.
Properness and the DM property are preserved by the representable proper universal curve.
acceptance: This induction does not assume the genus-one base.

Over M̄₀,₃ the inverse image of its empty boundary is empty, while the universal curve M̄₀,₄ has three boundary points coming from old-section collisions; an inverse-image-only boundary formula is wrong.

sources.locator: Theorem 2.7 proof, printed p.179 (PDF19), boundary-union formula and tᵢ↦xy chart
sources.match: The source treats separately the added old-section divisors and the inverse image of the old boundary. Properness and DM pass through the representable proper universal curve; its source smoothness does not follow from properness alone.

nodes.title: The rigid triangle locus
nodes.statement: Let E/Z be the ordered three-pointed genus-one curve of Knudsen II Figure 4: three rational components arranged in a cycle, with one smooth marking P₁,P₂,P₃ on each component. Glue P₁ to the marking of a stable one-pointed genus-one family F/S and retain P₂,P₃ as ordered markings. The resulting genus-two two-pointed family defines a closed immersion M̄₁,₁→M̄₂,₂ with uniquely recoverable labelled rational triangle. Étale locally its image is cut out by four distinguished node-smoothing parameters: the three internal triangle nodes and the attachment node. If F is nodal there is a fifth boundary parameter; that parameter is not set to zero on the image.
hypotheses: F/S is a stable ordered one-pointed genus-one family; E is the fixed split labelled triangle pulled back from Z.
The assertion about intersections is étale local with the four chosen branches distinguished; it is not an intersection of four globally embedded boundary components.
proofSteps: Use the parent external clutching pushout to attach F to E at its first marking; the triangle has Betti number one, so the glued genus is two. Each rational triangle component has exactly three special flags.

Recover the component containing P₂, the component containing P₃, and the unmarked connecting triangle component with its attachment flag. Prove this recovery on families and pointed isomorphisms, including when F is irreducible nodal; triviality of the automorphism group of the ordered triangle is only one part of this family comparison.

Use the higher-genus pointed deformation charts: dim M̄₂,₂=5, and impose the three internal smoothing parameters and the attachment smoothing parameter. Four independent equations leave relative dimension one. At a nodal F the remaining fifth parameter cuts out its boundary. The family recovery and closed-image argument are recorded in the rigid-locus gap, rather than inferred just from fibrewise rigidity.
acceptance: For smooth F there are four nodes, four irreducible components, vertex genera summing to one and graph Betti number one; the genus is two.
For irreducible nodal F there are five nodes, four rational normalization components and graph Betti number two; the genus is still two.
Three equations in the five-dimensional ambient stack would give relative dimension two and cannot describe M̄₁,₁.

sources.locator: Theorem 2.7 proof and Figure 4, printed p.179 (PDF19)
sources.match: The source counts the triangle attachment as well as its three internal nodes, and counts the genus-one nodal boundary as a fifth branch. Closed immersion is specific to this rigid labelled locus; the general separating clutching map is not thereby a closed immersion.

nodes.title: The one-pointed genus-one base stack
nodes.statement: M̄₁,₁ is a proper smooth Deligne–Mumford stack over Z of relative dimension one with relative normal-crossings boundary. Its rigid triangle-clutching realization in M̄₂,₂ is étale locally the intersection of four distinguished boundary branches. At a nodal one-pointed genus-one curve, the fifth ambient node-smoothing branch restricts to the boundary of M̄₁,₁.
hypotheses: The stack parametrizes stable one-pointed genus-one families, including irreducible nodal rational fibres; it is not the smooth elliptic locus alone.
proofSteps: Obtain the genus-at-least-two pointed stacks first by universal-curve induction, so the ambient M̄₂,₂ does not depend on this genus-one theorem.
Use the specific rigid triangle closed immersion and its family recovery, not the false general closed-immersion claim of Knudsen II Corollary 3.9(b).

On a smooth relative five-dimensional ambient chart, impose the four independent smoothing parameters from the rigid triangle and its attachment. The remaining relative parameter gives dimension one. Properness follows from the closed immersion into the proper ambient stack; the fifth branch at the nodal point gives the relative normal-crossings boundary.
acceptance: The smooth elliptic locus has one remaining deformation parameter after imposing four equations in relative dimension five.
The boundary parameter of an irreducible nodal genus-one curve remains free on the image; imposing it too would give only the boundary point.

sources.locator: Theorem 2.7 proof, printed p.179 (PDF19)
sources.match: The proof explicitly imposes four branches for M̄₁,₁ and a fifth only for its singular locus.

nodes.title: Deligne–Mumford–Knudsen theorem
nodes.statement: For every g,n≥0 with 2g−2+n>0, M̄_{g,n} is a smooth proper Deligne–Mumford stack over Z of relative dimension3g−3+n. The smooth substack M_{g,n} is open dense and its complement has relative normal crossings.
hypotheses: g,n are nonnegative integers in the explicitly stated stable range 2g−2+n>0; family bases are schemes.
Parent contraction/cohomology inputs have locally Noetherian scope until the separate approximation gap is discharged.
proofSteps: Induct on n using the universal-curve equivalence.
In a nodal chart replace the old smoothing coordinate t by uv; the total chart is smooth over Z and the boundary equation replaces t by the product uv.
Start separately at (0,3),(1,1), and (g,0) for g≥2. Properness and the DM diagonal pass through the representable universal curve.
acceptance: The relative dimension is0 at (0,3) and1 at both (0,4) and (1,1).

nodes.title: The cross-ratio compactification
nodes.statement: M₀,₄≅P¹_Z minus {0,1,∞} and M̄₀,₄≅P¹_Z. The three boundary points are precisely the three unordered2+2 partitions of the four ordered markings.
hypotheses: The fixed stable pair is (g,n)=(0,4), with four ordered labels; the construction is over Spec Z.
proofSteps: The universal curve over M̄₀,₃ is P¹ with its three sections.
Use expansion at the fourth section: outside the three sections the fourth coordinate is the cross-ratio; at the three sections it creates the corresponding stable two-component curve.
acceptance: The compactification adds three points, each with a stable rational tail.

nodes.title: Separating clutching morphism
nodes.statement: For ordered complementary marking sets I,J and g₁+g₂=g, with stable source pairs (g₁,|I|+1),(g₂,|J|+1), define ξ_{g₁,I}:M̄_{g₁,I∪{a}}×M̄_{g₂,J∪{b}}→M̄_{g,n} by gluing a and b in the disjoint union. The new node is distinguished in the construction, but is forgotten in the target. The two source components may each already be reducible.
hypotheses: All marking sets are finite and ordered/reindexed explicitly; every source vertex pair satisfies 2g_v−2+n_v>0.
The stack morphism is specified on arbitrary schemes; the parent coherent pushout proof over locally Noetherian bases requires the recorded extension for arbitrary bases.

Its arbitrary-base-change and isomorphism compatibility define the stack morphism.

uses.how: Both clutching morphisms are representable finite and unramified. For a fixed target stable curve their geometric fibres are finite choices of a node and, when relevant, an ordering or genus/marking assignment to its branches. These choices can be more than one even for a fixed separating genus and marking partition.

A pointed boundary type is a stable connected genus-g graph with n labelled legs and exactly one edge, up to label-preserving graph isomorphism, using the parent’s weighted dual graphs. Its compactified normalization parameter stack is the product of the vertex moduli stacks modulo the finite automorphism group of this graph. For n=0,g≥2 the types are Δ₀ and Δᵢ for1≤i≤⌊g/2⌋, where Δ₀ is the closure of the nonseparating one-node locus, not merely the locus of irreducible nodal curves.

Under ordered separating clutching, ξ*E_{g,n}≅pr₁*E_{g₁,n₁+1}⊕pr₂*E_{g₂,n₂+1}, hence ξ*λ_{g,n}≅pr₁*λ_{g₁,n₁+1}⊗pr₂*λ_{g₂,n₂+1}. The determinant comparison uses concatenated wedge bases in that order. Exchanging the two factors contributes the Koszul sign (−1)^{g₁g₂}; descent to a permitted graph-exchange quotient retains this action, rather than the ordinary unsigned symmetry of the two line factors alone.

The stack morphism is specified on arbitrary schemes; the parent coherent pushout proof over locally Noetherian bases requires the recorded extension for arbitrary bases.

nodes.title: Finite unramified clutching
nodes.statement: Both clutching morphisms are representable finite and unramified. For a fixed target stable curve their geometric fibres are finite choices of a node and, when relevant, an ordering or genus/marking assignment to its branches. These choices can be more than one even for a fixed separating genus and marking partition.
hypotheses: Use stable source and target pairs and the actual scheme clutching from parent Layer 3.
Relative singular loci in a smoothing need not be flat or étale over the base; only unramifiedness is used here.
proofSteps: An automorphism of the input mapping to the identity of the target restricts to the identity on its partial normalization, giving injectivity on stabilizers. Use the exact DM-stack representability criterion from the requested supplier.

Over a target family the fibre product records a persistent chosen node and ordered branch/marking/genus data, as in Knudsen’s auxiliary doubled stabilization argument. The relative singular locus is finite unramified for a proper nodal family, but generally not flat. The precise family representability and node-choice comparison is recorded as an open contract.

The representable morphism is quasi-finite by finite node choices. Properness follows from proper source and separated target over Z; proper plus quasi-finite gives finiteness. The node-choice factorization gives unramifiedness; none of these steps requires a closed immersion of the entire separating map.
acceptance: There can be two distinct separating preimages for two elliptic tails.

For xy=t over k[t], the relative singular scheme has coordinate ring k[t]/(t); it is finite unramified over k[t] but not flat. Do not replace the node-choice scheme by a finite étale cover over a smoothing base.

nodes.statement: A pointed boundary type is a stable connected genus-g graph with n labelled legs and exactly one edge, up to label-preserving graph isomorphism, using the parent’s weighted dual graphs. Its compactified normalization parameter stack is the product of the vertex moduli stacks modulo the finite automorphism group of this graph. For n=0,g≥2 the types are Δ₀ and Δᵢ for1≤i≤⌊g/2⌋, where Δ₀ is the closure of the nonseparating one-node locus, not merely the locus of irreducible nodal curves.
hypotheses: g,n≥0 with 2g−2+n>0; vertex genera are nonnegative integers; graph legs carry distinct fixed labels.
At each vertex 2g_v−2+val(v)>0, where valence counts both flags of a loop and all legs. Graph automorphisms act by relabelling the corresponding vertex markings.
proofSteps: Specialize the parent stable graphs to one edge and keep leg labels.
Use the parent normalization data and finite graph automorphisms to form the quotient parameter.
acceptance: Higher-node curves can lie on several branches of the same global boundary component.

uses.how: The normalization of the reduced total boundary of M̄_{g,n} is the disjoint union, over stable one-edge types, of the corresponding vertex-product quotient stacks. Its finite map to the boundary records a distinguished node; it separates branches at curves with several nodes of the same type.

For π:M̄_{g,n+1}→M̄_{g,n} and retained i, let D_{i,n+1} be the divisor of a rational tail carrying exactly marks i,n+1 and its attachment. Then Lᵢ on the source is π*Lᵢ⊗O(D_{i,n+1}); equivalently π*Lᵢ=Lᵢ⊗O(−D_{i,n+1}).

For g≥2 let Δ be the effective Cartier divisor M̄_g minus M_g, with coefficient1 on each reduced local node branch. Its global decomposition is Δ=Σ_{i=0}^{⌊g/2⌋}Δᵢ according to the one-edge unpointed types. For a generically smooth stable family over an integral noetherian S, its pullback is an effective Cartier divisor Δ_S; arbitrary families mapping entirely into Δ do not have this effective-Cartier pullback.

nodes.title: Normalization of the boundary
nodes.statement: The normalization of the reduced total boundary of M̄_{g,n} is the disjoint union, over stable one-edge types, of the corresponding vertex-product quotient stacks. Its finite map to the boundary records a distinguished node; it separates branches at curves with several nodes of the same type.
hypotheses: Use the full stable range, reduced total boundary and compactified vertex stacks; no quotient coarse spaces replace these stacks.
The graph quotient is by the constant finite automorphism group acting on vertex factors and flag labels. Characteristic two is included without using μ₂ or averaging.
proofSteps: Use finite representable clutching and its invariant descent through the constant graph automorphism group. The product of vertex stacks is smooth and normal; its finite-group quotient is normal as a stack because the torsor atlas is étale, including in characteristic two.

On the one-node stratum, partial normalization recovers the vertex data uniquely up to graph automorphisms, including automorphisms on objects. Check this as an equivalence of groupoids, not just uniqueness of geometric points. Local nodal smoothing charts show the same map separates the branches at a curve with several nodes.

Use the stack normalization universal property after an étale atlas, with finite birational comparison and effective gluing. R09.5 names normalization but does not specify this stack-level theorem: the exact owner extension is a recorded gap. The characteristic-zero descriptions in Hacking and CLP do not fill the integral supplier gap.
acceptance: The map is not globally an isomorphism onto a smooth boundary divisor.

Each is an invertible sheaf because the marking is in the relative smooth locus; it identifies with sᵢ*Ω¹_{C/M̄}. Base change and relabelling preserve this line. The class ψᵢ=c₁(Lᵢ) is an exported input to the consumer’s tautological Chow-ring construction, not a new Chow theory here.

Use the parent relative dualizing sheaf and its base-change isomorphisms with the actual stack descent.

Use its agreement with relative differentials on the smooth locus and its base-change cocycle to descend a line on the stack.

The line identity is integral. Hacking’s explicit source statement is characteristic zero; extending it over Z uses the nodal coordinate and stack descent contract recorded as a gap.
proofSteps: Work on a versal nodal deformation chart xy=t with the selected boundary branch t=0. Its conormal is generated by t modulo t².

For changes of branch parameters x′=ux+higher terms and y′=vy+higher terms, the first-order smoothing class t′ modulo t² transforms by u₀v₀. The branch differential frames transform by u₀ and v₀; identify the conormal with their tensor. Prove independence from the higher-order terms via the node deformation module, rather than checking only linear rescalings.

Branch exchange sends x,y to y,x and preserves xy=t, so the conormal exchange is the usual unsigned tensor symmetry, including characteristic two. Check all graph-equivariance and atlas/base-change cocycles. The exact integral deformation-line/descent contract remains a recorded gap; the characteristic-zero reference is not silently generalized.

For x′=ux and y′=vy, the conormal generator transforms by uv, whereas the dual normal generator transforms by (uv)⁻¹.

They are initial for maps to algebraic spaces and induce bijections between geometric points and isomorphism classes. Stable coarse spaces are proper over Z. Existence alone gives neither smoothness of the coarse space nor a universal family on it; base change is used only with the hypotheses of the imported coarse-space theorem.
hypotheses: The full range, base and auxiliary data are specified in the statement; none are suppressed by a global stable-pair convention.
proofSteps: The finite diagonal gives finite inertia; apply the generic coarse-space existence theorem with its noetherian finite-type hypotheses.
Use the proper coarse-space comparison to deduce properness.
Restrict the stable coarse space to the saturated smooth open; geometric curve smoothness is invariant under isomorphism.

Otherwise split persistent nodes after a finite cover of B and use the normalization residue sequence.

Its kernel is the direct sum of component bundles twisted by (m−1)D^ν, nef by the pointed theorem, and its quotient is a direct sum of O_B. Apply preservation of nefness under extensions from the positivity supplier.

nodes.statement: Let S be a noetherian scheme and f:X→S a stable genus-g family with g≥2. nodes.statement: For g≥2 M̄^{coarse}_g is a projective scheme over Z. There is a positive power of a sufficiently high pluricanonical determinant which descends to an ample line on the coarse algebraic space.
hypotheses: The full range, base and auxiliary data are specified in the statement; none are suppressed by a global stable-pair convention.

The composite cover→coarse is proper with finite geometric fibres, hence finite; a proper algebraic space with a finite surjective scheme cover can be treated by finite ampleness descent.
Use coarse descent of sufficiently divisible powers of line bundles; no injectivity of equivariant Picard into ordinary Picard is asserted.

Apply the finite-degree-equations node once to the universal stable family on the single proper finite-type scheme cover over Z. Relative Serre generation of its ideal sheaf and vanishing give a common d for which the multiplication quotient is surjective and its degree-d equations determine every geometric fibre, in every characteristic. Its ideal sheaf is flat over the base because the ambient projective bundle and stable family are flat, so these generating equations remain equations of each fibre.

For this fixed d, apply the determinant-ampleness argument on every geometric fibre of the cover over Spec Z: its precise multiplication/classifying-map conditions are already satisfied. Fixed-line openness of relative ampleness then gives neighbourhoods covering Spec Z. Thus this one determinant power is relatively ample everywhere. No maximum of varying fibrewise exponents is taken.
An ample line on the proper coarse algebraic space makes it a projective scheme.

nodes.title: Full symplectic level on smooth curves
nodes.statement: Fix g≥2 and N≥3 invertible on the base. A full homogeneous Jacobi level on a smooth genus-g curve is a group-scheme isomorphism α:(Z/N)^{2g}→J(C)[N] whose transported Weil pairing is the standard alternating form through some isomorphism Z/N≅μ_N. Fixing a primitive root ζ_N specifies a base Z[1/N,ζ_N] and the symplectic subfunctor with that exact pairing. The homogeneous functor over Z[1/N] has its induced primitive-root/multiplier morphism; after choosing ζ_N its symplectic-similitude frames separate according to the multiplier. The exact symplectic component and the whole similitude functor are distinct, not equivalent moduli problems after forgetting the choice.
hypotheses: g≥2; N≥3 is invertible on every test base. The fixed symplectic flavour includes a chosen primitive root ζ_N; the homogeneous flavour retains its multiplier.

The JC1 suppliers initially construct smooth projective geometrically connected families over Noetherian bases. General test families require the tricanonical Noetherian atlas, arbitrary pullback and effective polarized-abelian descent specified below; no field theorem is used as family representability.
proofSteps: On the Noetherian smooth-curve tricanonical atlas from MC.1/hilbert-quotient import JC1/relative-jacobian and JC1/principal-polarization. JC1/jacobian-base-change supplies arbitrary, including nonreduced, pullbacks of this family.

Descend these actual polarized abelian schemes along the curve-family atlas, using functorial curve isomorphisms and their all-test-scheme cocycle. The precise arbitrary-base descent bridge is an R09.4 request; the accepted Noetherian JC1 statements do not by themselves prove it.

Use A3 prime-to-characteristic torsion and Weil pairing and M6 symplectic frames. Define the pairing-preserving isomorphism functor and curve-level isomorphisms. For the DM H¹ étale formulation retain the separate SF.3 cup-product/Tate-twist/dual comparison; a Jacobian existence theorem does not fix that convention.
acceptance: N is invertible; level at the characteristic is a different problem.

For ξ_irr there is an exact sequence0→E_{g−1,n+2}→ξ_irr*E_{g,n}→O→0 with the last map the residue at an ordered branch. It gives ξ_irr*λ_g≅λ_{g−1,n+2}. Exchanging the two branches negates the residue; the induced equivariant determinant data must retain this sign when descending to the unlabelled graph quotient.

Over C, for the universal stable genus-g family with g≥2, 12c₁(λ)=f_*(c₁(ω)²)+[Δ] in codimension-one Chow groups with rational coefficients, equivalently the corresponding Picard identity modulo torsion after the line-valued Deligne-pairing comparison. Each universal node smoothing branch contributes coefficient1. The integral identity over Z is proved separately by complex torsion freeness and the integral Picard injection, not by an unstated mixed-characteristic GRR theorem.

For g≥2 there is an isomorphism of invertible sheaves on M̄_{g,Z}:λ^{⊗12}≅⟨ω,ω⟩⊗O(Δ). The relative Deligne pairing is a line on the base; its first Chern class is f_*(c₁ω·c₁ω). This is an integral Picard-group identity, natural under classifying pullback.

For g≥2 and N≥3 over the fixed pairing base B=Spec Z[1/N,ζ_N], let τ:M_g[N]→A_g[N] be smooth full-level Torelli. The canonical comparison of its universal families identifies τ* of the ppav Hodge bundle with f_*ω of the universal curve; its determinant identifies τ* of the ppav Hodge line with the curve Hodge line. Pullback along every T→M_g[N], including nonreduced T, respects these comparisons and their identity/composition isomorphisms.

Over an algebraically closed field k, the coarse stable curve moduli admits a morphism t̄:M̄_g^{coarse}→A_g^{min} extending smooth Torelli. On a stable curve it uses the abelian part of the generalized Jacobian and maps to the corresponding minimal-compactification stratum. The descended rational Hodge line satisfies λ_coarse=t̄*ω_min, with ω_min ample.

Let k be a field, S̄ normal integral projective over k, and f:X̄→S̄ a stable genus-g family g≥2 with smooth restriction over a dense open S. If that smooth family has maximal variation, λ_{S̄}=det f_*ω is nef and big. No maximal-variation conclusion is asserted for an isotrivial positive-dimensional family.

nodes.title: Rational Noether identity
nodes.statement: Over C, for the universal stable genus-g family with g≥2, 12c₁(λ)=f_*(c₁(ω)²)+[Δ] in codimension-one Chow groups with rational coefficients, equivalently the corresponding Picard identity modulo torsion after the line-valued Deligne-pairing comparison. hypotheses: The full range, base and auxiliary data are specified in the statement; none are suppressed by a global stable-pair convention.
proofSteps: Work on the characteristic-zero smooth tricanonical moduli charts with the equivariant descent needed for the stack. The universal curve is regular; its relative nodal morphism is lci, with its cotangent complex and virtual relative tangent convention specified.
In the universal node chart xy=t, Ω¹→ω has cokernel at the codimension-two singular locus. Compute the node term and descend the branch contribution.

nodes.title: Torsion freeness of the stable-stack Picard group
nodes.statement: For g≥2 Pic(M̄_{g,C}) is torsion free. A torsion line gives a finite cyclic cover of the stack. Over Teichmüller space this cover splits; its character factors through the mapping-class group, and extending over every boundary kills each Dehn-twist generator, so the cover and line are trivial.
hypotheses: The full range, base and auxiliary data are specified in the statement; none are suppressed by a global stable-pair convention.
proofSteps: The proof uses connected simply connected Teichmüller space, the analytic presentation of the smooth stack and generation by Dehn twists. These general analytic inputs have no verified atlas supplier and are recorded as gaps.
Use the one-node smoothing monodromy to identify the boundary loop with the corresponding Dehn twist.
Since the cover extends over that divisor, its cyclic monodromy on the loop vanishes; all generators vanish.
acceptance: Retain stack stabilizers; passing first to the coarse space is not this proof.

nodes.title: Graph-closure compactification after a finite cover
nodes.statement: Choose a projective compactification S̄₀ of S and the normal projective finite scheme cover V→M̄_g. Let W=S×_{M̄_g}V, choose a reduced irreducible component W₀ dominating S, and normalize it to S′. The map W→S×V is finite, as the pullback of the finite diagonal of M̄_g. It need not be a monomorphism: the chosen isomorphism of the two curve families is part of W.
Close its finite image in the projective product, preserving the S̄₀-coordinate and then its function field K(W₀); normalization in a finite extension is finite over the excellent finite-type base.
Because W₀ is finite over its image, normalization over the open S in K(W₀) is the normalization of W₀; the extension family is obtained from the second projection to V.
