nodes.title: The smooth full-level Torelli morphism
nodes.statement: Over the fixed pairing base and for g≥2, form τ:M_g[N]→A_g[N] by the relative Jacobian with its canonical principal polarization and induced full level. The pullback of the universal abelian scheme is canonically Jac(C_g/M_g[N]); in particular the square of abelian schemes is Cartesian.
hypotheses: g≥2 and N≥3; work over B=Spec Z[1/N,ζ_N] in the fixed symplectic component, with the same pairing convention in M_g[N] and A_g[N].
The fine curve scheme is Noetherian, and its universal curve is smooth projective geometrically connected of genus g; hence the JC1 suppliers apply without choosing a section of the curve.
proofSteps: Apply the exact JC1/relative-jacobian, JC1/jacobian-base-change and JC1/principal-polarization imports to the universal curve over the Noetherian fine scheme. All satisfy g>0, smoothness, projectivity and geometric connectedness. Arbitrary test-scheme pullbacks are supplied by their base-change comparisons.

Equip this relative Jacobian with the given torsion frame and apply the M5/M6 fine ppav universal property over the identical cyclotomic base. The classifying map and its universal-family identification give the Cartesian square.
acceptance: The curve-to-Jacobian construction is not AbelianSchemes duality.

For the Hodge API use MC.6/jacobian-hodge-comparison; no generic Picard Lie or curve duality theorem is reconstructed here. Do not import JC7/universal-level-jacobian: that application itself depends on this roadmap’s full-level and fine-level nodes.

sources.match: DGH §6.1 constructs the curve-level Torelli map and Cartesian square in a chosen characteristic-zero level component. The integral base application uses exact JC1 and M5/M6 supplier contracts, whose transitive gaps remain open.

api.name: CurveTorelli.map
api.statement: τ sends (C,α) to (J(C),λ_C,α).

api.name: CurveTorelli.cartesian
api.statement: τ* of the universal ppav is the relative Jacobian of the universal curve.

api.name: CurveTorelli.hodge
api.statement: τ* of the ppav Hodge determinant is det f_*ω of the curve family.

api.name: CurveTorelli.baseChange
api.statement: Change of base over the fixed pairing base commutes with τ and its universal-Jacobian comparison through the relative Picard base-change isomorphism; identity and composition satisfy the same cocycle.

tests.name: CurveTorelli.dimension
tests.statement: In genus2 both smooth moduli and ppav moduli have dimension3.

tests.name: CurveTorelli.minusLevel
tests.statement: For nonhyperelliptic genus≥3, (C,α) and (C,−α) can be distinct curve-level objects although their ppav-level images are isomorphic.

tests.name: CurveTorelli.hyperelliptic
tests.statement: The hyperelliptic involution realizes sign change of level on the curve.

uses.how: On geometric points the smooth full-level Torelli morphism has fibres of size at most2. On nonhyperelliptic curves the two objects (C,α) and (C,−α) are distinct for N≥3; for hyperelliptic curves they are isomorphic. Since every smooth genus-two curve is hyperelliptic, the genus-two map is injective on geometric points. Finite fibres do not imply the smooth Torelli map is a finite morphism.

For g≥2 and N≥3 over the fixed pairing base B=Spec Z[1/N,ζ_N], let τ:M_g[N]→A_g[N] be smooth full-level Torelli. The canonical comparison of its universal families identifies τ* of the ppav Hodge bundle with f_*ω of the universal curve; its determinant identifies τ* of the ppav Hodge line with the curve Hodge line. Pullback along every T→M_g[N], including nonreduced T, respects these comparisons and their identity/composition isomorphisms.

nodes.title: Finite Torelli fibres and the sign ambiguity
nodes.statement: On geometric points the smooth full-level Torelli morphism has fibres of size at most2. On nonhyperelliptic curves the two objects (C,α) and (C,−α) are distinct for N≥3; for hyperelliptic curves they are isomorphic. Since every smooth genus-two curve is hyperelliptic, the genus-two map is injective on geometric points. Finite fibres do not imply the smooth Torelli map is a finite morphism.
hypotheses: The full range, base and auxiliary data are specified in the statement; none are suppressed by a global stable-pair convention.
proofSteps: Import strong classical Torelli: a ppav isomorphism of Jacobians equals ± the Jacobian of a curve isomorphism, with the hyperelliptic qualification.
Apply the pairing-level compatibility; on a nonhyperelliptic curve there is no curve automorphism inducing −1.
For genus2 use the hyperelliptic double cover. All named classical curve/Jacobian facts require the proposed owner extension.
acceptance: The blanket claim of noninjectivity for every g≥2 is excluded.

sources.locator: Theorem 12.1(a)–(b), printed/PDF p.38; uniqueness/sign proof pp.38–39; proof of (a) §13, pp.40–45
sources.match: Strong Torelli identifies a ppav isomorphism up to sign and a curve isomorphism; the two signs give distinct curve-level objects exactly outside the hyperelliptic locus. The main proof and general owner extension remain open.

sources.locator: §6.1, printed/PDF p.24, paragraph following diagram (6.1)
sources.match: Asserts finite-to-one on C-points, rather than a finite morphism. The at-most-two and hyperelliptic refinements follow from the strong Torelli statement, not from this finite-fibre assertion alone.

nodes.title: Hodge pullback along smooth full-level Torelli
nodes.statement: For g≥2 and N≥3 over the fixed pairing base B=Spec Z[1/N,ζ_N], let τ:M_g[N]→A_g[N] be smooth full-level Torelli. The canonical comparison of its universal families identifies τ* of the ppav Hodge bundle with f_*ω of the universal curve; its determinant identifies τ* of the ppav Hodge line with the curve Hodge line. Pullback along every T→M_g[N], including nonreduced T, respects these comparisons and their identity/composition isomorphisms.
hypotheses: The fine-level scheme and its universal smooth projective curve have the MC.4/fine-level-scheme properties; g≥2, N≥3 invertible, with the same ζ_N pairing component on both moduli schemes.

JC6 supplies the generic stable-family comparison over integral Noetherian bases with g>1. Apply it componentwise on the regular Noetherian fine curve scheme using the explicit SF.0 component criterion; do not silently apply that supplier over an arbitrary nonintegral base.
proofSteps: The fine curve scheme is regular Noetherian and quasi-compact. Use the requested SF.0 statement that such a scheme is a finite disjoint union of open-and-closed integral connected components. This avoids requiring the separate Teichmüller/level-connectedness theorem merely to use JC6.

On each component the universal smooth curve is a stable connected nodal family of genus g>1. Import JC6/curve-jacobian-hodge-bundles and JC6/hodge-line-isomorphism; their generic Lie/duality construction stays in the Jacobian owner.

The Cartesian abelian-family comparison of smooth-torelli identifies the invariant differentials with the pullback ppav Hodge bundle. Assemble the componentwise isomorphisms on their disjoint cover and take the determinant.

Pull back the resulting universal comparison to arbitrary T by the supplied Hodge-bundle and Jacobian base-change isomorphisms. Check identity/composition; no new arbitrary-base Picard representability theorem is inferred from the integral-base JC6 statement.
acceptance: This is a canonical algebraic line comparison; metric equality is supplied by the Arakelov owner.

sources.locator: Lemma3.4 and proof,pp.43–44
sources.match: Yuan Lemma3.4 is explicitly for stable genus g>1 families over integral Noetherian S, and its proof uses the Picard Lie comparison and relative duality. This node is the moduli-specific pullback application of the exact JC6 supplier, not a second generic family comparison.

nodes.title: The compactified Torelli and Hodge comparison
nodes.statement: Over an algebraically closed field k, the coarse stable curve moduli admits a morphism t̄:M̄_g^{coarse}→A_g^{min} extending smooth Torelli. On a stable curve it uses the abelian part of the generalized Jacobian and maps to the corresponding minimal-compactification stratum. The descended rational Hodge line satisfies λ_coarse=t̄*ω_min, with ω_min ample.
hypotheses: The full range, base and auxiliary data are specified in the statement; none are suppressed by a global stable-pair convention.
proofSteps: On integral Noetherian stable-family atlas charts import R11.4/stable-family-picard and JC6/hodge-line-isomorphism. The source does not require a regular total space. Descending the semiabelian group and line comparisons to the stack remains part of the atlas/descent contract. For a geometric stable curve use R11.4/normalization-exact-sequence to identify the abelian quotient with the product of normalized-component Jacobians; the torus retains loops and multiple edges.

Use the minimal Siegel extension theorem and descended rational automorphic Hodge line; the all-characteristic unlevel statement needs a scoped supplier extension, not an unsupported assertion from good-prime level moduli.
Check the extension and line comparison on the boundary with the source’s abelian-part interpretation and descent.

The DVR-only R11.4/picard-zero is not an arbitrary stable-family supplier. The normalization node’s own DVR-shaped predecessor and G-normalization-cohomology gap remain an external composition boundary; its accepted statement alone is not proof closure. MC.6/jacobian-hodge-comparison now applies to smooth full-level Torelli, so the stable boundary comparison imports JC6 directly.
acceptance: The entire semiabelian Jacobian is not an abelian scheme at a non-compact-type node.

sources.locator: §6, printed pp.210–211 (PDF pp.11–12), characteristic-zero Satake map and properties (1)–(2) on p.211
sources.match: The source is characteristic zero; it states the boundary abelian-part interpretation and Hodge pullback after a modular-form tensor power. The all-characteristic extension is a recorded supplier gap.

sources.locator: §3.4, printed/PDF p.56, compactified Torelli/Hodge paragraph
sources.match: Uses the all-field compactified map and ample rational Hodge line, citing Faltings–Chai. Those inputs must be source-checked and descended at a prime-to-characteristic level; finite fibres on the smooth locus suffice for the bigness application.

nodes.title: Nef and big Hodge line for maximal variation
nodes.statement: Let k be a field, S̄ normal integral projective over k, and f:X̄→S̄ a stable genus-g family g≥2 with smooth restriction over a dense open S. If that smooth family has maximal variation, λ_{S̄}=det f_*ω is nef and big. No maximal-variation conclusion is asserted for an isotrivial positive-dimensional family.
hypotheses: The full range, base and auxiliary data are specified in the statement; none are suppressed by a global stable-pair convention.
proofSteps: After a finite field or level-cover change use the compactified Torelli and ample rational Hodge line on the minimal Siegel compactification.
The composite classifying map is generically finite onto its image by maximal variation and finite Torelli fibres.
The pullback of an ample line along a projective generically finite map is nef and big; descend nefness/bigness through the finite cover.
acceptance: Only finite fibres on the smooth locus are used.

sources.match: The cited passage supplies the construction or proof in the stated range; qualifications and upstream inputs are explicit in the statement and prerequisites.

nodes.title: The degree-d level Picard parameter functor
nodes.statement: For g≥2, N≥3 invertible with a fixed ζ_N pairing component, and d∈Z, define P_g,N^d=Pic^d_{C_g/M_g[N]} on the fppf site. This represented smooth quasi-projective degree-d sheaf is a torsor under the relative Jacobian, parametrizing sheafified relative line classes on the universal smooth curve. An algebraically closed field point corresponds to an isomorphism class of triples (C,α,L). For a general T→M_g[N], lifting a sheaf point to an actual degree-d line bundle is controlled by the boundary to H²_fppf(T,G_m); when it vanishes, the line-bundle isomorphism classes lifting that point form a torsor under Pic(T) by base pullback. The triple groupoid and this sheaf are distinct.
hypotheses: g≥2, N≥3 invertible and d an arbitrary integer; the fixed pairing component is over Z[1/N,ζ_N].

The universal curve lies over the Noetherian fine scheme and is smooth projective with geometrically connected genus-g fibres, so JC0 representability and torsor statements apply. For every test base T, use O_T≅(f_T)_*O_{C_T} universally from the specified parent stable-family/cohomology contract before applying the exact obstruction and kernel statements.
proofSteps: Apply JC0/relative-degree-components, JC0/picard-representability and JC0/picard-torsors to the universal curve on its Noetherian fine base. Representability and all arbitrary-base-change identifications use the imported A0-extension Picard sheaf, not global representatives.

Verify the universal global-functions isomorphism for the proper flat smooth geometrically connected family, then apply JC4/actual-to-relative-obstruction to every pullback C_T/T. Its exact sequence is 0→Pic(T)→Pic(C_T)→Pic_{C_T/T}(T)→H²_fppf(T,G_m)→H²_fppf(C_T,G_m). Restrict the lifting assertion to the degree-d component.

Exactness gives existence when the boundary vanishes and the Pic(T)-torsor of lifts, using injectivity of base pullback. A chosen curve section kills the boundary and permits the A0-extension/section-picard-split rigidification; no section of the unpointed universal curve is assumed.

Over algebraically closed k, choose an fppf-local actual line representative. A nonempty finite-type open of the covering scheme has a k-point, whose pullback supplies an actual line on C_k; thus the boundary of every relative point vanishes. Pic(k)=0 makes the lift class unique. Full-level rigidity controls the curve-level isomorphism; scalar line automorphisms survive in the groupoid.

Use JC6/picard-lie-cohomology on a constant smooth genus-two family over C for the dual-number test, together with the exact arbitrary-pullback Picard comparison. The infinitesimal calculation is imported, not re-planned here.
acceptance: The Picard parameter is a sheaf of classes, not the automorphism groupoid of line bundles.

sources.locator: §4.3.2, printed/PDF pp.73–75; representability and geometric triples, pp.74–75
sources.match: Defines the degree-d curve-level-line triples and the relative Picard parameter. The manuscript only needs the algebraically closed field comparison; general-base line lifting remains the specified Picard-owner input.

sources.locator: §9.3 Theorem1 and proof p.252; §8.1 Leray discussion p.203 and Proposition4 pp.204–205
sources.match: Representability/torsors apply on the Noetherian universal base. The exact obstruction sequence needs universal global functions; cohomological H²_fppf is not an asserted Azumaya identification.

api.name: LevelPicardParameter.fiber
api.statement: The fibre over a smooth curve-level point is its degree-d Picard scheme.

api.name: LevelPicardParameter.torsor
api.statement: Picᵈ is a torsor under the relative Jacobian; there need not be a canonical origin.

api.name: LevelPicardParameter.obstruction
api.statement: For p∈P^d(T) the Leray boundary δ(p)∈H²_fppf(T,G_m) vanishes exactly when an actual degree-d line bundle on C_T represents p, under O_T≅(f_T)_*O_{C_T} universally. The cohomological group is not identified with Azumaya classes without an additional theorem.

api.name: LevelPicardParameter.baseChange
api.statement: Over any T→M_g[N], pullback of P_g,N^d represents the fppf degree-d Picard sheaf of C_T/T, with canonical identity/composition comparisons; no universal line is inferred.

api.name: LevelPicardParameter.tensor
api.statement: Tensor product gives P^d×_{M_g[N]}P^e→P^{d+e}; O is the degree-zero unit and dualization P^d→P^{−d} gives the inverse. The degree-zero action on P^d is the stated Jacobian torsor action.

api.name: LevelPicardParameter.liftFiber
api.statement: If δ(p)=0, tensoring any lift L by f_T*M identifies the set of line-bundle isomorphism classes lifting p with a Pic(T)-torsor. Two lifts differ by a unique base line-bundle class. For a field Pic(T)=0 this set is a singleton; general bases need not have that uniqueness.

tests.name: LevelPicardParameter.degreeZero
tests.statement: For d=0 the relative Picard component is the Jacobian with its canonical origin.

tests.name: LevelPicardParameter.sectionRigidification
tests.statement: A chosen section permits rigidification and a Poincaré line; the unpointed universal family is not assumed to have that section.

tests.name: LevelPicardParameter.scalarInertia
tests.statement: The groupoid of triples has G_m scalar automorphisms of L; it cannot be identified with the represented Picard sheaf as a groupoid.

tests.name: LevelPicardParameter.canonicalDegree
tests.statement: The dualizing line of the universal smooth curve determines a canonical section of P^{2g−2}; a canonical section of P¹ is not inferred from full level alone.

tests.name: LevelPicardParameter.baseTwist
tests.statement: Take T=P¹_C, a constant smooth genus-two curve C with fixed symplectic level3, and any degree-d line L on C. The lines pr_C*L and pr_C*L⊗pr_T*O(1) are distinct on C×T, as restriction along a C-point distinguishes them, but give the same point of the relative degree-d Picard sheaf. This rejects a parameter functor of unquotiented global line classes.

tests.name: LevelPicardParameter.dualNumbers
tests.statement: For a fixed smooth genus-two curve over C with symplectic level3 and degree-d line L, first-order relative Picard deformations over C[ε]/(ε²) reducing to [L] form a torsor under H¹(C,O_C), a two-dimensional C-vector space. The constant lift chooses an origin. This rejects a functor keeping only reduced geometric points.

uses.how: For an algebraically closed field k in which N is invertible, geometric points of P_g,N^d identify with isomorphism classes of curve-level-line triples. For general bases retain the fppf sheafification and the obstruction/rigidification distinction; the existence of the parameter scheme does not produce a tautological line on every pulled-back curve.

nodes.title: Geometric triples and the Picard sheaf
nodes.statement: For an algebraically closed field k in which N is invertible, geometric points of P_g,N^d identify with isomorphism classes of curve-level-line triples. For general bases retain the fppf sheafification and the obstruction/rigidification distinction; the existence of the parameter scheme does not produce a tautological line on every pulled-back curve.
hypotheses: g≥2, N≥3 and d∈Z as in the parameter node; k is algebraically closed with N invertible, and the fixed pairing primitive root is part of the level datum. General-base remarks use the parameter node’s universal global-functions hypothesis.
proofSteps: Use the represented degree-d relative sheaf and JC4/actual-to-relative-obstruction. Over algebraically closed k a local fppf representative lifts to an actual line by choosing a k-point in a nonempty finite-type open of its covering scheme. Hence its Leray boundary vanishes. Pic(k)=0 makes the actual line class unique. This gives the bijection without reconstructing general Brauer cohomology theory here.

Use MC.4/level-rigidity to identify curve-level representatives uniquely up to their prescribed isomorphism; passage to line-bundle classes removes scalar inertia. For general bases, boundary vanishing only gives existence, and base Picard twists still give multiple actual line classes.
acceptance: Scalar automorphisms disappear only after passage to classes.

sources.locator: §4.3.2, printed/PDF p.75, first two paragraphs
sources.match: The stated bijection is explicitly for algebraically closed fields; the additional general-base obstruction distinction is an imported Picard-sheaf contract, not a assertion of a universal line bundle in this passage.

nodes.title: Nefness with smooth generic fibre
nodes.statement: Let f:X→B be a family of nodal curves of genus g≥2 over a smooth projective curve over an algebraically closed field, with smooth generic fibre. For m≥2, f_*ω^m is nef.
hypotheses: The full range, base and auxiliary data are specified in the statement; none are suppressed by a global stable-pair convention.
proofSteps: Resolve the isolated rational double points crepantly and preserve pluricanonical pushforwards. Treat contraction of smooth exceptional curves separately; it is not the false pullback identity noted in source issue E9.

After finite base covers arrange base genus≥2. In characteristic p>0, iterate Frobenius to make a negative line quotient f_*ω^m→M^{-1} have arbitrarily negative degree; write M=ω_B^m⊗L with L very ample.
The quotient gives H¹(B,L⊗ω_B^m⊗f_*ω^m) of dimension≥g(B)≥2. Projection formula and the low-degree Leray injection give H¹(X,ω_X^m⊗f*L) of dimension≥2 on a smooth minimal general-type surface.

Choose a reduced union D of smooth fibres in |f*L|. Its connected components have genus≥2 and O(D)|_D is trivial. Apply the Mumford–Ekedahl bound to the positive twist ω_X^m(D): zero except possibly p=2,m=2, where the dimension is≤1.

Use finite-cover nef descent and spreading of the negative quotient to positive characteristic. Rational-double-point resolution, general type, contraction, vanishing and spreading are exact surface-owner inputs recorded as gaps.
acceptance: The exceptional surface bound is sufficient; it is not claimed to be zero.

sources.locator: Proposition6.3 and Lemmas6.4–6.5,pp.23–26
sources.match: The cited passage supplies the construction or proof in the stated range; qualifications and upstream inputs are explicit in the statement and prerequisites.

nodes.title: Nonnegative dualizing degree along a section
nodes.statement: Let B be a smooth projective connected curve over an algebraically closed field and f:X→B a proper flat finitely presented family of geometrically connected nodal curves of arithmetic genus g≥2, with smooth generic fibre. For every section s:B→X through the relative smooth locus, deg(s*ω_{X/B})≥0.
hypotheses: Use the smooth-generic direct-image nef theorem for m≥3; no stability assumption on every fibre and no special-fibre vanishing for ω^m(−s) are imposed.

The parent supplies relative duality and generic pluricanonical generation; the SF.0 owner extension supplies the invertible evaluation image/effective-divisor comparison on the smooth integral base curve.
proofSteps: Choose m≥3. On the smooth generic fibre, ω^m is globally generated, so evaluation f_*ω^m→s*ω^m is generically surjective.
On the smooth integral base curve B the image is an invertible sheaf I=s*ω^m(−D) for an effective divisor D. It is a locally free quotient of the nef bundle f_*ω^m, hence deg I≥0.
Thus m deg(s*ω)=deg I+deg D≥0. No vanishing of R¹f_*(ω^m(−s)) on every special fibre is used: an unstable rational tail can make it nonzero.
Use torsion-free sheaves on a nonsingular curve, saturation/effective-divisor comparison and nef quotient positivity from the stated owner extension.
acceptance: For the blowup of a smooth genus≥2 family at a special-fibre point, a section on the exceptional rational tail still has nonnegative dualizing degree.

On a genus≥2 curve with an attached rational tail containing s, Serre duality gives nonzero H¹(ω^m(−s)) for m≥2: the dual ω^{1−m}(s) has sections supported on the tail and vanishing at the attaching point. The proof must survive this failure of the former vanishing claim.

sources.locator: Corollary 6.6, printed/PDF p.25 (statement and proof)
sources.match: States nonnegative intersection with a section. For an arbitrary nodal family, replace the proof’s asserted R¹-vanishing by the generic-evaluation/image argument in proofSteps; an unstable rational tail supplies the recorded nonvanishing guard.

nodes.title: Nefness on pointed normalization components
nodes.statement: Let f:X→B be a nodal family over a smooth projective algebraically closed field curve with smooth connected generic fibre, and s_i disjoint smooth-locus sections. For integers m≥2 and 0≤a_i≤m, f_*ω^m(Σa_i s_i) is nef, including a zero direct image in the negative-degree genus-zero cases.
hypotheses: The full range, base and auxiliary data are specified in the statement; none are suppressed by a global stable-pair convention.
proofSteps: Use the source-scoped resolution and contraction comparison to reduce to the smooth-surface models used in Proposition 6.7, retaining 0≤a_i≤m so pushforward comparisons through exceptional curves have the required nonnegative exceptional coefficients.

For genus≥2 begin with the smooth-generic nef theorem. The section increment has adjunction quotient (s_i*ω)^{m−a_i−1} with nonnegative exponent and degree. Justify the direct-image sequence on the reduced model; do not assert fibrewise R¹-vanishing on an arbitrary unstable original nodal family.

For genus0, the direct image is zero when Σa_i<2m. Once Σa_i≥2m, Hodge index for the disjoint sections allows an increment with nonpositive self-intersection; adjunction gives a nonnegative quotient degree.

For genus1 with a section use the elliptic-fibration canonical-bundle formula and nonnegative χ from Euler/Noether. If there are no sections, supply a finite base change acquiring one and descend nefness.
Exact vanishing/direct-image transport on these models, genus0/1 surface inputs and finite-cover descent remain the existing surface/positivity-owner gaps.
acceptance: This is a positivity statement for vector bundles, not just numerical degree of their determinants.

sources.locator: Proposition 6.7, printed/PDF pp.25–27, statement p.25 and three genus cases pp.26–27
sources.match: The coefficients satisfy 0≤a_i≤m with m≥2. The surface resolution/contraction and genus-zero/one arguments are needed in addition to the genus≥2 direct-image theorem and remain the surface-input gap.

nodes.title: Direct-image sequence at persistent nodes
nodes.statement: After a finite base change splitting the horizontal nodes of a stable family X/B, normalize along them, ν:X^ν→X, and let D^ν be the two branch divisors. Then ν*ω_{X/B}≅ω_{X^ν/B}(D^ν). For m≥2 there is an exact sequence 0→(fν)_*ω_{X^ν/B}^m((m−1)D^ν)→f_*ω_{X/B}^m→f_*O_D→0, with f_*O_D a direct sum of copies of O_B.
hypotheses: The full range, base and auxiliary data are specified in the statement; none are suppressed by a global stable-pair convention.
proofSteps: Use the parent conductor/dualizing comparison and the antidiagonal gluing condition on the two branch values. Adjunction gives ω_{X^ν/B}(D^ν)|_{D^ν}≅O_{D^ν}.
The componentwise pointed vanishing gives the direct-image exact sequence and its base-change ranks.
Descend the two branch quotients to the one O_D quotient using the antidiagonal condition; retain the signs in the m-th tensor power.
acceptance: The residue sequence concerns a persistently nodal generic fibre; isolated special-fibre nodes use the smooth-generic theorem.

sources.locator: Lemma 6.8, printed/PDF pp.27–28; Proposition 6.9, p.28, exact sequences
sources.match: Normalization separates the persistent branches; the power-m branch gluing is (-1)^m, and after splitting node/branch sections the quotient is O_D. Stable-pointed vanishing, rather than arbitrary nodal vanishing, supplies surjectivity after pushforward.

nodes.title: Naturality of section evaluation
nodes.statement: Let A be any commutative ring, γ,δ,s,t∈A, q=X²+γXY+δY², R=A[Y][X]/(q(X,Y)−q(s,t)), u=[X], v=[Y], ι:A→R, c=u−ιs, d=v−ιt, b=u+ιs+ιγ·ιt, a=ιδv+ιδ·ιt+ιγu, J=(c,d), D=Hom_R(J,R), m(r)(j)=rj, ev:R→A the section evaluation and ε the unique dual generator dε(j)=bj. For f:A→A′, primes denote the same construction with mapped parameters and φ:R→R′ the coefficient map. ev′(φ(r))=f(ev(r)) for every r∈R.
hypotheses: All coefficient rings are commutative and may have zero divisors or be the zero ring. No noetherianity, unit discriminant, injectivity or flatness of f is required. Statements concern the explicit polynomial model, not arbitrary nodal families.
proofSteps: Both sides are ring maps R→A′; evaluate them on u, v and every coefficient ιz.
Use the unique expression p(v)+u q₁(v) to reduce the equality to coefficientwise polynomial evaluation.

The checked native proof compares the two ring maps by AdjoinRoot.ringHom_ext; their values on coefficient polynomials and the root agree. This direct proof uses neither the admitted sectionEvaluationKernel body nor a flatness assumption.
acceptance: The equation holds also when f kills a nonzero coefficient; it is not cancellation through f.

sources.locator: §3, printed pp.11–12, monic division and the dual residue calculation preceding Proposition3.1
sources.match: The maps below are authored tensor and quotient adapters for the explicit monic calculation. Their arbitrary-ring range follows by normal-form cancellation, rather than by invoking the printed stably reflexive proposition outside its noetherian/unit-discriminant hypotheses. No completed-local or geometric conclusion is inferred.

nodes.title: Algebraic tensor comparison for a pointed node
nodes.statement: Let A be any commutative ring, γ,δ,s,t∈A, q=X²+γXY+δY², R=A[Y][X]/(q(X,Y)−q(s,t)), u=[X], v=[Y], ι:A→R, c=u−ιs, d=v−ιt, b=u+ιs+ιγ·ιt, a=ιδv+ιδ·ιt+ιγu, J=(c,d), D=Hom_R(J,R), m(r)(j)=rj, ev:R→A the section evaluation and ε the unique dual generator dε(j)=bj. For f:A→A′, primes denote the same construction with mapped parameters and φ:R→R′ the coefficient map. Construct the unique A′-algebra equivalence E_R:A′⊗_A R≃R′ with E_R(a′⊗r)=ι′a′·φ(r). The tensor algebra multiplication is (a′⊗r)(b′⊗z)=a′b′⊗rz.
hypotheses: All coefficient rings are commutative and may have zero divisors or be the zero ring. No noetherianity, unit discriminant, injectivity or flatness of f is required. Statements concern the explicit polynomial model, not arbitrary nodal families.
proofSteps: The coefficient map is an A-algebra map after restricting the target through f; its scalar equation follows on coefficients.
Use the baseline algebra base-change universal property to obtain the A′-algebra map with the specified pure-tensor formula.
The existing linear tensor comparison has the same formula, hence the same underlying map by tensor induction. Transfer its inverse/bijectivity, not an unproved algebra isomorphism.
Uniqueness follows by equality on pure tensors.
acceptance: Multiplication preservation is required; an unrelated A′-linear normal-coordinate identification does not suffice.

nodes.title: Canonical tensor comparison for the section dual
nodes.statement: Let A be any commutative ring, γ,δ,s,t∈A, q=X²+γXY+δY², R=A[Y][X]/(q(X,Y)−q(s,t)), u=[X], v=[Y], ι:A→R, c=u−ιs, d=v−ιt, b=u+ιs+ιγ·ιt, a=ιδv+ιδ·ιt+ιγu, J=(c,d), D=Hom_R(J,R), m(r)(j)=rj, ev:R→A the section evaluation and ε the unique dual generator dε(j)=bj. For f:A→A′, primes denote the same construction with mapped parameters and φ:R→R′ the coefficient map. Construct the canonical A′-linear equivalence E_D:A′⊗_A D≃D′ characterized by E_D(a′⊗h)(φ(j))=ι′a′φ(h(j)). It is identity-compatible and composition-compatible under the canonical heterobasic base-change cancellation a″⊗(a′⊗h)↦a″g(a′)⊗h: for g:A′→A″, E_{D,g}(a″⊗E_{D,f}(a′⊗h))=E_{D,gf}(a″g(a′)⊗h).

proofSteps: Identify the mapped-polynomial quotient in the existing tensor theorem with R′ by coefficientwise mapping of the explicit polynomial; transport the ideal and dual through that equality.
Pure-tensor evaluation determines the dual map because φ(c),φ(d) generate J′ as an R′-ideal; do not assume φ(J) is all of J′ as a set.
For the identity, compare evaluations on c,d. For composition, evaluate the two nested maps on φ_gφ_f(c),φ_gφ_f(d), and use coefficient-map composition.

nodes.statement: Let A be any commutative ring, γ,δ,s,t∈A, q=X²+γXY+δY², R=A[Y][X]/(q(X,Y)−q(s,t)), u=[X], v=[Y], ι:A→R, c=u−ιs, d=v−ιt, b=u+ιs+ιγ·ιt, a=ιδv+ιδ·ιt+ιγu, J=(c,d), D=Hom_R(J,R), m(r)(j)=rj, ev:R→A the section evaluation and ε the unique dual generator dε(j)=bj. The current native proof applies the existing target-coordinate regularity to the two characterized corrections. The named canonical specialization is also proved by the two actual ideal-valued naturality lemmas. Neither proof uses the unproved dual tensor equivalence.

nodes.statement: Let A be any commutative ring, γ,δ,s,t∈A, q=X²+γXY+δY², R=A[Y][X]/(q(X,Y)−q(s,t)), u=[X], v=[Y], ι:A→R, c=u−ιs, d=v−ιt, b=u+ιs+ιγ·ιt, a=ιδv+ιδ·ιt+ιγu, J=(c,d), D=Hom_R(J,R), m(r)(j)=rj, ev:R→A the section evaluation and ε the unique dual generator dε(j)=bj. Equip A′⊗_A D with the canonical module structure over the actual tensor algebra T=A′⊗_A R, uniquely characterized by (a′⊗r)·(b′⊗h)=a′b′⊗(r·h). This specializes the existing module/tensor universal properties, and introduces no new abstract theory of tensor representations.
hypotheses: All coefficient rings are commutative and may have zero divisors or be the zero ring. No noetherianity, unit discriminant, injectivity or flatness of f is required. Statements concern the explicit polynomial model, not arbitrary nodal families.
proofSteps: The displayed product is additive and A-balanced separately in both pairs, using the coefficient scalar tower on D; extend it by the tensor universal property.
Check unit, associativity and both distributivities on pure tensors and extend by tensor induction.
In the normal coordinates of D, use r·(z,α)=(rz+ιαK(r),ev(r)α). This checks that the tensor action is not the componentwise action on R⊕A.

nodes.title: Semilinear coefficient map on the section ideal
nodes.statement: Retain R=AdjoinRoot(X²+C(γY)X+C(δY²−q(s,t))), ι:A→R, u=[X], v=[Y], c=u−ιs,d=v−ιt,b=u+ιs+ιγ·ιt, J=(c,d)=ker(ev), and the existing canonical projection p(r)=r−ιev(r) and dual generator ε:J→R with dε(j)=bj. Let R′,J′,p′,ε′ denote the same native objects with mapped coefficients, and φ:R→R′ the existing coefficient map induced by AdjoinRoot.map. Construct the actual φ-semilinear restriction ψ:J→J′, whose underlying ring value is ψ(j)=φ(j). It sends the two ordered ideal generators to their corresponding primed generators, satisfies ψ(rj)=φ(r)ψ(j), and obeys identity and composition on actual ideal elements. This restriction is not asserted injective or an equivalence; the tensor equivalence is a separate existing obligation.
hypotheses: A and A′ are arbitrary commutative rings, including the zero ring; γ,δ,s,t∈A and f:A→A′ is any unital ring homomorphism. No flatness, injectivity, noetherianity or unit-discriminant hypothesis is imposed. Statements concern the untruncated explicit polynomial model, not arbitrary nodal families.
proofSteps: Naturality of ev sends every j∈ker(ev) into ker(ev′), hence into the native J′.
Restrict the native ring homomorphism to the two native ideal subtypes; use its additive and multiplicative equations for the built semilinear LinearMap structure.
The existing coefficient projection formulas give the two generator values. The native ring-map identity and composition prove the pointwise identities by subtype extensionality.
A nonflat coefficient map can annihilate a nonzero ideal element; do not infer a pure-map inverse from a later tensor comparison.
acceptance: Underlying carrier is the native Ideal.span subtype, not a new quotient or tensor carrier.
Semilinearity uses φ on R-scalars; f-linearity without scalar transport would be ill-typed.

nodes.statement: Let A be any commutative ring, γ,δ,s,t∈A, q(X,Y)=X²+γXY+δY², R=A[Y][X]/(q(X,Y)−q(s,t)), ι:A→R the coefficient algebra map, u=[X], v=[Y], J=(u−ιs,v−ιt) and D=Hom_R(J,R). All duals are R-linear and use native Module.Dual. For any A-module M put N_M=R⊗_A M with its inherited left R-action and η=Module.Dual.eval R J. The canonical exchange Φ_D,M:D∨⊗_A M≃ₗ[R]Hom_R(D,N_M) is an equivalence with Φ_D,M(F⊗m)(h)=F(h)⊗m. Construct it as (η⁻¹⊗id_M) followed by the existing Θ_J,M.

Tensor induction gives uniqueness and naturality for every A-linear map M→M′.
